sentences.text: ORAL ORDER

Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award rendered in MACP No.73 of 2006 dated 24/07/2012 by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Amreli allowing the claim to the tune of Rs.96,004/- with 9% interest and cost against the respondent no.1 and exonerated the insurance company, present appeal is filed by org. claimant.
2. Though served, none appears for the respondents.

3. Having heard the learned advocate for the appellant and examining the R & P, what could be noticeable that learned tribunal awarded Rs.96,004/- on the ground that driver of the offending vehicle was not having endorsement to drive the transport vehicle on the date of road accident.
The effect of the endorsement to drive the transport vehicle was expired much prior to the road accident and therefore insurance company could not held liable to indemnify the risk of the owner.

Believing that riding transport vehicle without having endorsement is fundamental breach of the terms and conditions of the policy, the tribunal has exonerated the insurance company from liability to pay the compensation.

Paragraph 46 deals with the said aspect which reads thus:
"46. Section 10 of the Act requires a driver to hold a licence with respect to the class of vehicles and not with respect to the type of vehicles.
In one class of vehicles, there may be different kinds of vehicles.
If they fall in the same class of vehicles, no separate endorsement is required to drive such vehicles.
As light motor vehicle includes transport vehicle also, a holder of light motor vehicle licence can drive all the vehicles of the class including transport vehicles.
It was pre-amended position as well the post- amended position of Form 4 as amended on 28.3.2001.

Any other interpretation would be repugnant to the denition of "light motor vehicle" in section 2(21) and the provisions of section 10(2)(d), Rule 8 of the Rules of 1989, other provisions and also the forms which are in tune with the provisions.

Even otherwise the forms never intended to exclude transport vehicles from the category of `light motor vehicles' and for light motor vehicle, the validity period of such licence hold good and apply for the transport vehicle of such class also and the expression in Section 10(2)(e) of the Act `Transport Vehicle' would include medium goods vehicle,
medium passenger motor vehicle, heavy goods vehicle, heavy passenger motor vehicle which earlier found place in section 10(2)
(e) to (h) and our conclusion is fortied by the syllabus and rules which we have discussed.

Thus we answer the questions which are referred to us thus:
(i) `Light motor vehicle' as defined in section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in section 2(21) read with section 2(15)
and 2(48).

and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg. or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight"
of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form.

(iii) The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act No.54/1994 w.e.f. 14.11.1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in section 10(2)(e), medium passenger motor vehicle in section 10(2)(f), heavy goods vehicle in section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in section 10(2)(h) with expression `transport vehicle'
as substituted in section 10(2)(e) related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.
It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of section 10(2)(d) and section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

(iv) The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle" continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect."
5. The above ratio is squarely applicable to the facts of the case.
The finding of the tribunal exonerating the insurance company is failed to sustain.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The opponents are are held liable to pay the compensation jointly and severally.

The org. claimant is entitled to recover the compensation of Rs.96,004/- with 9% interest from the date of filing of the petition till its realization and cost jointly and severally from the opponents.

The respondent No.2 - insurance NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3729/2012 ORDER DATED: 06/02/2025 undefined company is directed to deposit the awarded amount within six weeks from the date of the receipt of the writ of this order.

Upon deposit of such amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque / NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
The tribunal concerned shall inform the insurance company about passing of this order.
